subject: Mutual Action Plan: token/unit-econ sanity sweep & evaluation timeline
messages:
From: Sam Green <sam.green@medalhealth.com>
To: grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, jordan_blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@medalhealth.com
Date: 2027-04-26T13:12:00Z
Subject: MAP kickoff — unit economics sanity sweep + evaluation timeline

Hi Grace / Jordan,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team was impressed. Before we commit to the pilot/PO we need to lock down a couple of MAP items that are blocking procurement: a short unit-econ sanity sweep and a concrete evaluation timeline. Specifically we need: 

- Your tokens-per-dollar assumptions for the model variants you recommended (including quantized variants).
- Expected latency impact at different batching sizes (1, 4, 8) and a recommended latency SLO.
- Caching/prefetch expectations: what hit-rate should we plan for if we warm session prefixes vs no warm cache?
- A short evaluation plan (pilot length, pass/fail criteria, sample traffic needed) and an estimated close timeline once those pass.

I attached a small sample of our traffic profile (medalhealth_traffic_sample.csv) so you can start. Can you respond with a short checklist and an ETA for the MAP doc so procurement can schedule the PO review?

Best,
Sam
Sam Green
Director, Product Integrations
MedalHealth

Attachments: medalhealth_traffic_sample.csv (csv)
From: grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Sam Green <sam.green@medalhealth.com>
Cc: jordan_blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-26T14:03:00Z
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff — unit economics sanity sweep + evaluation timeline

Thanks Sam — received and this is exactly the kind of clarity we want in the MAP. Quick checklist from our side so procurement has clear inputs: 

1) Traffic intake: we’ll use the attached sample as the baseline for simulations; if you have 24-hr peak vs median splits that helps.
2) Token assumptions: we’ll provide tokens/$ across the 3 model variants you saw (base fp16, 8-bit quantized, and a trimmed small-LLM) with per-token costs for hosted vs dedicated.
3) Batching & latency: we’ll run simulated latency curves at batch sizes 1 / 4 / 8 given your P95 SLO target — we need to know acceptable P95 (suggest <250ms as starting point).
4) Caching: we’ll provide prefix cache hit-rate scenarios: conservative (5%), expected (20%), aggressive (45%) and show unit-cost impact.
5) Eval plan & timeline: proposal below — happy to adjust.

Proposed short evaluation plan (draft):
- Week 0 (MAP signoff): agree on traffic sample + acceptance criteria
- Week 1–2 (canary): 48hr canary against pilot environment (10% traffic) to validate latencies and token accounting
- Week 3–4 (pilot): 2-week pilot with production traffic (throttled to agreed throughput), metric checks weekly
- Post-pilot: procurement PO and go/no-go within 5 business days assuming no regressions

ETA: we can produce the cost/econ appendix + simulation artifacts by EOD Tuesday (2027-04-28) if that timeline works. Can you confirm the P95 SLO and whether procurement needs an itemized cost table for hosted vs dedicated?

Thanks — Grace
Grace O'Connor
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, jordan_blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Sam Green <sam.green@medalhealth.com>
Date: 2027-04-26T15:10:00Z
Subject: RE: MAP kickoff — token/unit-econ quickcalc + assumptions (internal + to client)

Internal + client-facing notes below — flagged items in bold. Deal ID MH-4381.

Summary (short):
- Baseline token price (hosted API, mid-size) = $0.0009 / token for fp16 base at our published rate; quantized path reduces inference-cost by ~18–28% depending on perf slippage.
- If customer picks Dedicated (reserved pool) per-token unit costs drop further ~22% at moderate commitments.

Key assumptions for simulations:
- Model variants: base-fp16 (recommended for quality), 8-bit-quant (good tradeoff), small-trim (for bulk low-variability calls).
- Batch sizing: batch=1 median latency 120ms, batch=4 +35ms overhead, batch=8 +70ms; P95 inflation depends on queuing — simulate 95th tail for each profile.
- Cache assumptions: prefix cache hit-rate scenarios to model: low=5%, base=20%, high=45%. Cache primarily benefits multi-turn workflows where prefixes repeat.
- Tokenization: our token-count model uses tiktoken-like estimator; plan to attach quickcalc.

Operational recommendations (for MAP):
- Use a canary with batch=1 to validate latency SLO before enabling batching on pilot.
- If P95 SLO is <=250ms, we recommend conservative batching (<=4) and aggressive prefetch warming to hit >20% cache.
- For financials, present three scenarios to procurement: Nominal (base pricing + base cache 20%), Optimistic (quant + dedicated + high cache 45%), Conservative (no cache + base pricing).

Attachments: token_econ_quickcalc.xlsx (internal calc) — will export a client-facing PDF with tables by EOD Tuesday.

Action items: 
- Grace: send confirmed P95 target to Sam.
- Jordan: draft the MAP milestone table with the procurement line items (PO timing, billing cadence).
- I’ll run a short sim that shows tokens/$ sensitivity to cache hit-rate and batch size by EOD Tuesday.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Inference Engineer | Redwood Inference

Attachments: token_econ_quickcalc.xlsx (xlsx)

Subject: Re: MAP kickoff — unit economics sanity sweep & evaluation timeline

Sam — following on Grace/Karthik’s points, here’s a compact MAP timeline and procurement checklist you can share internally: 

MAP milestones (proposed):
- MAP signoff (day 0): agree traffic baseline and P95 acceptance (owner: MedalHealth)
- Cost appendix delivery (day +2): Redwood delivers tokens/$ table for three scenarios + PDF summary (owner: Redwood)
- Canary window (day +7): 48h canary at 10% traffic to validate latency and token accounting (owner: Redwood ops + MedalHealth eng)
- Pilot (day +14 to +28): 2-week pilot at agreed throughput (owner: MedalHealth product + Redwood)
- Procurement PO (target day +31): PO submitted and billing cadence agreed (owner: MedalHealth procurement)

Procurement checklist (short):
- Itemized hosted vs dedicated cost table (we’ll provide)
- SLA targets and crediting language (we’ll propose standard SLA in the MAP)
- Pilot acceptance criteria: P95 within agreed target, <2% error rate, tokens-per-transaction within agreed tolerance

Meeting: I’m available Thursday 2027-04-29 10:00–11:00 PT to walk procurement + product through the appendix. Does that time work for you? If not, propose an alternative and we’ll adapt.

Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
